title: The Echo of New Lagos
premise: Odile Zhou, a clone of a murdered detective, arrives at New Lagos to close a case the original never solved and finds a colony quietly dying of engineered memory decay. The distress signal in a dead language turns out to be a broadcast from the original Odile herself, recorded before her death, revealing that the colony's corporate overlords erased New Lagos to hide a massacre. To prevent two fleets from destroying each other over the truth, Odile must sustain a fabricated ceasefire broadcast until the jump window opens. In the end she exposes the massacre, lets the original's identity die with the lie, and chooses to remain in New Lagos as its recorder rather than return as anyone's echo.
about_author: August Blackwood is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing colonial records before turning to fiction. They write slow-burning science fiction about people who outlive their own histories.

chapters.title: The Colony That Forgot Itself
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Arriving in New Lagos, Odile interviews witnesses who cannot remember the original's murder and discovers the colony's memory clinics are scrubbing decades of records. The emotional beat is quiet unease: everyone smiles, no one remembers, and Odile realizes they are investigating a crime inside a mind being erased in real time.

chapters.title: A Language With No Speakers
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The distress signal decodes into pre-Exodus Yoruba-English creole, and its voiceprint matches the original Odile Zhou. Following its source into the flooded archive district, Odile finds the original's hidden recordings documenting the massacre the corporation buried. The beat is dread turning into resolve: the case was never cold, only silenced.

chapters.title: The Lie That Holds Two Fleets
chapters.summary: Alternating between Odile and corporate executive Marek Adeyemi's POV. Both fleets arrive demanding the truth; Odile broadcasts the original's fabricated ceasefire to keep them apart, while Marek works to expose the forgery and trigger a war that would bury the evidence forever. The beat is vertiginous tension as the jump window closes and the lie begins to fray.

chapters.title: What the Echo Keeps
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. In the climax, Odile broadcasts the massacre recordings during the final minutes of the jump window, shattering the ceasefire but forcing both fleets to witness the truth instead of destroying each other over its absence. Marek falls with his secrets. The resolution is grief and release: Odile stays in New Lagos, no longer the original's echo but the colony's memory keeper.
